benchmarks_captured: ...plus one row per benchmark's own name/fullName for every benchmark page on the site (409 benchmark pages on 2026-09-03, up from 406 on 2026-09-02) - same benchmark catalog family as 20260902/benchlm/meta.json (AA AIME 2025, AA-LCR, SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, etc.), not re-listed in full here to keep this file short; see normalized.json for the exact set of "benchmark" values captured today.
extraction_method: chrome-devtools MCP: opened https://benchlm.ai in an isolated-context tab (isolatedContext=benchlm-rescrape-20260903), read __NEXT_DATA__ for the current buildId, then fetched the site's own SSG data endpoints /_next/data/euf_1hAZlYZlUaI_uldoX/{index,models,benchmarks,llm-pricing,llm-speed,frontier-ai-models,llm-price-performance}.json plus /_next/data/euf_1hAZlYZlUaI_uldoX/benchmarks/<slug>.json for all 409 benchmark slugs and /_next/data/euf_1hAZlYZlUaI_uldoX/models/<slug>.json for all 410 model slugs (slug lists taken from sitemap-0..17.xml, 89,394 <loc> entries scanned). All fetches issued from the page's own fetch() inside evaluate_script, saved straight to disk via the filePath option; no DOM scraping needed except to confirm __NEXT_DATA__.buildId.
notes: No XHR/fetch data API exists beyond /api/market (unrelated market blurb, not captured). All leaderboard data ships in Next.js SSG payloads, saved verbatim in raw.json.

raw.json holds the untouched pageProps for every benchmark page, every model page and the index/models/pricing/speed pages. On the 410 model-detail payloads the keys comparisonLinks, faqs, visuals, seo, radar and peerPosition were dropped before saving (site now nests model data one level deeper under pageProps.pageData; those six keys were dropped from pageData and the remainder unwrapped to pageProps.pageData directly, matching the flat shape used in 20260902/benchlm/raw.json) to keep file size down; every other field is verbatim.

The homepage leaderboard ships as tuple-encoded arrays (39 columns, no column names in the payload) inside pageProps.homepageData.leaderboard.rows (nested one level deeper than 20260902, which had the rows array directly under pageProps.homepageData.leaderboard). Verified against a handful of rows: [1]=model, [2]=slug, [3]=provider, [8]=contextWindow, [10]=inputPrice, [11]=outputPrice, [12]=blendedPrice, [13]=tokensPerSecond, [14]=latency seconds, [15]=Elo, [17]=release date, [26]=displayScore, [27]=full-precision overall score, [30]=category scores array in order Agentic,Coding,Reasoning,Multimodal & Grounded,Knowledge,Multilingual,Instruction Following,Math. Same mapping as 20260902.
rank for per-benchmark records is the position in the leaderboard order the site publishes for that benchmark (no numeric rank field in the payload), same convention as 20260902.

rank for Overall was computed by sorting the 230 scored models by full-precision overall score (row[27]) descending; score reported is the rounded displayScore (row[26]), matching the 20260902 convention.

cost_usd, context_window and date on every record prefer the model's own detail-page values (pricing.blendedPrice, pricing.contextWindow, model.releaseLabel parsed to ISO) and fall back to the per-benchmark leaderboard row's own contextWindow, or to the homepage row's blendedPrice/contextWindow/release-date columns for Overall/Category/Elo records. Fields are omitted (not fabricated as null/0) when no source has a value.

Benchmark name collisions exist across slugs; source_url disambiguates (benchmark pages use https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/<pageSlug>; Overall records use https://benchlm.ai/models/<slug>; Category records use https://benchlm.ai/<categoryKey>; Elo records use https://benchlm.ai/).

No values were estimated or invented. Missing data is omitted. Zero fetch errors; all 409 benchmark and 410 model endpoints returned HTTP 200 on first or second attempt (some evaluate_script calls had to be retried because other agents scraping other sites concurrently in the same shared browser session repeatedly reselected/renavigated this tab between the select_page and evaluate_script calls; every retry was preceded by a location.href check that aborted the script instead of fetching on the wrong site).
